symptom: On an MPR v1 project (unit contents inside the .mpr, Mendix below 10.18) a unit write replaced Unit.Contents and left Unit.ContentsHash describing the old bytes, and an inserted unit got ContentsHash ''. `mx check` 0 errors and MxBuild clean; Studio Pro reads the hash to detect what changed. `mxcli fix hashes` said v1 'has no index to drift' and exited 0
cause: The v2 branches of updateUnit, WriteTransaction.WriteUnit and insertUnit computed base64(SHA-256) and stored it; the v1 branches wrote `UPDATE Unit SET Contents = ?` and `INSERT … ContentsHash = ''`, on the assumption that the column only indexes mprcontents files. It does not: Studio Pro fills it on every v1 unit too
file: `modelsdk/mpr/writer_core.go` (v1 branches of `updateUnit`, `WriteTransaction.WriteUnit`, `insertUnit` now set ContentsHash = `contentsHashOf(contents)`), `modelsdk/mpr/contents_hash.go` (`verifyContentsHashesV1`, report `Version`, issue `Unit`), `cmd/mxcli/cmd_fix_hashes.go` (`reportV1Hashes`; the exec/docker drift warning still skips v1); tests `modelsdk/mpr/writer_v1_contents_hash_test.go`, `contents_hash_test.go`, `cmd/mxcli/cmd_fix_hashes_test.go`; repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/1159-mpr-v1-contents-hash.mdl`
insight: **Measure the formula on a Studio Pro-authored v1 file before writing it**: a fresh `mxcli new --version 9.24.30.51827 --skip-build` app stores standard padded base64 of SHA-256 over the Contents blob exactly, 308 of 308 units, and `testdata/v1-project/App.mpr` 20 of 20, so that fixture doubles as the control (`TestV1FixtureHashesMatchContents`). Platform run: the old binary left 2 stale rows after `create entity` + `create microflow` (DomainModel old hash, new microflow ''), the fixed one 0; `fix hashes --repair` repairs the stale copy. **The reporter's `add jar dependency` cannot reproduce on 9.24** (JarDependencies is 10.0+, refused up front), so use any rewrite plus any insert. **Testing WriteTransaction.WriteUnit on v1 through `NewWriter` hangs forever**: the reconcile reads the stored bytes through the reader's pool while the transaction holds its only connection (`SetMaxOpenConns(1)`), which on v1 (bytes in the same DB) deadlocks in `GetRawUnitBytes`. That is a separate defect of codec.Store.SaveUnit/FlushUnits on v1; the test uses an unlimited pool. **Keep the per-exec drift warning v2-only**: verifying v1 reads every blob in the .mpr (140 MB on a large app), and nothing but a writer can make a v1 row drift
